governing_policy: Government of India Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 (MoEFCC / CPCB) & Punjab Municipal SWM Implementation Rules

preparation_steps: Empty and rinse container thoroughly to remove food residues
Remove caps and lids (can be recycled together if clean)
Flatten bottles to conserve space

CONDITIONAL RULE FOR TAKEAWAY CONTAINERS: Rigid plastic food containers are accepted in Blue Bin ONLY if rinsed completely clean of food grease. Heavily oil-caked containers or foam clamshells must go to General Trash
Rinse food tins and drink cans
Clean aluminium foil is accepted; heavily food-caked foil goes to General Trash
Aerosol cans: ensure completely depressurized before placing in bin
Do NOT place batteries in this bin — batteries are Domestic Hazardous
Flatten corrugated shipping boxes to save space
Remove excessive shipping tape and staples
Keep dry — wet cardboard loses fiber structure

CONDITIONAL RULE FOR PIZZA BOXES & MEAL CARTONS: Clean dry cardboard lids with zero oil can be recycled in Blue Bin. Portions saturated with grease, cheese, or food oils cannot be hydrapulped and must go to General Trash (Black/Grey Bin)
Empty and rinse bottles and jars
Do not mix with ceramics, mirrors, or window glass (different melting points)
Remove metal lids and recycle separately with Metal
glass.safety_warning: ⚠️ SAFETY REQUIREMENT: If glass is broken, wrap securely in several layers of thick newspaper and label clearly before placing in collection to prevent injury to sanitation workers.

preparation_steps: Keep clean and dry — wet paper cannot be repulped
Remove plastic bindings or sleeves from documents
Do NOT include used facial tissues, soiled napkins, or thermal receipts
Includes non-recyclable composite packaging: multi-layer snack/crisp packets (metallized BOPP film), expanded polystyrene (Styrofoam cups/clamshells), and plastic straws/cutlery
Includes heavily food-contaminated packaging: greasy pizza boxes and food-soiled meal cartons where oil/grease cannot be cleaned off
Includes inert sweepings, cigarette butts, tangled ropes/strings, and outdoor non-recyclable litter fragments
For standard non-sanitary residual waste: bag securely and place into the Black or Grey Bin (Landfill / RDF)

SANITARY & SPECIAL-CARE EXCEPTION: If the detected object is a used tissue, paper napkin, disposable glove, diaper, or personal hygiene item, DO NOT dispose loose in regular general waste. Wrap securely in newspaper or paper pouch, mark with a prominent RED dot or cross, and hand over separately to municipal collectors per MoEFCC/CPCB SWM 2026 rules
general_trash.safety_warning: ⚠️ SANITARY & SPECIAL-CARE ADVISORY: If this detected item is a used tissue, napkin, disposable glove, or personal hygiene item, DO NOT throw loose into the general waste bin. Statutory municipal guidelines require sanitary items to be wrapped securely in newspaper or paper pouch, marked with a distinctive RED cross or dot, and handed over separately to sanitation staff for high-temperature incineration.

preparation_steps: Includes kitchen food leftovers, fruit & vegetable peels, eggshells
Includes tea leaves, coffee grounds, and garden trimmings
Do NOT bag in conventional plastic bags — use compostable bags or transfer loose
Never mix with plastic packaging, glass, or batteries

sanitary_waste.bin_color_india: Special Paper Pouch with Red Mark
preparation_steps: MANDATORY MUNICIPAL PROTOCOL: Used tissues, napkins, diapers, and sanitary pads must be wrapped securely in newspaper
Mark prominently with a RED cross or dot on the package
Hand over separately to municipal collection staff — NEVER mix into bulk recyclables
sanitary_waste.safety_warning: ⚠️ BIO-HAZARD RISK: Do not dispose sanitary waste in recycling or open bins. Always wrap securely in paper with a red marking.

preparation_steps: Store in a dry location out of reach of children
Deliver to authorized electronics retailers, battery kiosks, or municipal hazardous waste drop-offs
NEVER incinerate or dump in regular bins — toxic heavy metals poison groundwater
battery.safety_warning: ⚠️ TOXIC & FIRE HAZARD: Lithium and lead-acid batteries can cause severe fires or chemical contamination if placed in regular waste.
